secs.t: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 - sections → subject

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2023 keyed "Arrears of taxes - Section 50" as the correct match.
Exam angle: "What is covered under Part II / Part XII?" Answers: Reorganisation of the State; amendment of Articles 371D and 168.

Section 26 concerns delimitation; Section 46 concerns the Finance Commission award and related grants; Sections 84-85 concern the Apex Council and River Management Boards; and Section 90 concerns Polavaram.
The Thirteenth Schedule contains commitments relating to Central institutions and infrastructure for Andhra Pradesh, including an IIT, IIM, AIIMS, a new railway zone, a steel plant and a port.
Section 26
contains the delimitation-related provision under which the proposed Assembly strengths were to be increased from 175 to 225 in Andhra Pradesh and from 119 to 153 in Telangana.
Section 46 deals with the division of the Finance Commission award, grants and a package for backward areas, including Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 amended Section 5 to recognise Amaravati as
the sole and permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh with effect from 2 June 2024
Part I contains the preliminary provisions, including definitions and the population ratio of 58.32:41.68 based on Census 2011.
Part V concerns expenditure and revenue distribution; Part VII concerns certain corporations; Part IX concerns water resources; and Part X concerns infrastructure and special economic measures.
All four statements correctly state the population ratio and the statutory bases for apportioning assets, commercial undertakings, tax arrears and tax refunds.
For Schedule IX corporations under Section 53, operational units were allocated by location, while headquarters were allocated according to the population ratio.

secs.t: Bifurcation dates - Act, assent, appointed day, Telangana's rank

x: The Bill was passed first by the Lok Sabha, then by the Rajya Sabha, received presidential assent, and finally came into operation on the appointed day.
The Bill was introduced on 13 February 2014, passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on 18 and 20 February, received assent on 1 March, and bifurcation took effect on 2 June 2014.

secs.t: Post-bifurcation disputes - river boards, water, Polavaram ordinance, legal challenges

x: The
Krishna and Godavari
are the principal rivers involved in post-bifurcation water-sharing disputes between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
Section 108 empowers the Centre to remove difficulties, but it and the related expert committees do not prescribe deadlines or possess binding force.
Telangana has argued that the link violates the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal Award of 1980.

secs.t: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 - Schedules and apportionment basis

x: The Ninth Schedule covers PSUs and corporations, the Tenth State institutions, the Eleventh irrigation projects, and the Twelfth coal, oil, gas and power.
The Thirteenth Schedule contains promises relating to education and infrastructure, including provision for a railway zone, now identified as South Coast Railway.
Schedule IX units were divided according to location, while headquarters were divided according to the population ratio.
Tax refunds followed the population ratio, while power sharing used five-year average consumption; Andhra Pradesh received 46% of power for 58% of the population.

secs.t: Seats allocated → successor state

x: Section 30 provided for the common High Court at Hyderabad until
a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was established under Article 214
The judges’ salaries of the common High Court were shared according to the population ratio of Andhra Pradesh to Telangana, namely
Under Section 30, judges' salaries in the common High Court were split according to the
population ratio

secs.t: New states → year of formation

x: Exam angle: ascending-order questions - AP (1953/56) → Haryana (1966) → Chhattisgarh (2000) → Telangana (2014).
Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states in 1972 under the
North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971
Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states in 1972, while Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh were made Union Territories.
Size and governance are identified as newer considerations, since very large states such as Uttar Pradesh may become unwieldy to administer.
The formation of Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960 followed the
Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat movements
under the Bombay Reorganisation Act.
Subhash Ghisingh
founded the GNLF in 1980 and coined the term ‘Gorkhaland’.

The sequence is 1907 demand, 1980 foundation of the GNLF and coinage of ‘Gorkhaland’, 1988 formation of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council, and 2011 formation of the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration.
Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand
were created in 2000, with regional backwardness being an important consideration rather than linguistic identity.

secs.t: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

x: Exam angle: amendment number (32nd), date of President's Rule (Jan 1973), and which article gave the Central University (371E).
Exam angle: APHQ 2019 asked which amendment brought in the Six-Point Formula - the
32nd

Clause 1 concerned continuation and application of the Mulki Rules; Clause 3 localised the first two gazetted posts; Clause 4 concerned educational facilities; and Clause 5 concerned police recruitment.
The Six-Point Formula abolished the Mulki Rules and Telangana Regional Committee, introduced local preference in specified direct recruitment, and provided a special tribunal for promotion disputes.
The extension of Mulki rules to Assistant Surgeons and Engineers in 1972 sparked the
Jai Andhra agitation
The 32nd Amendment Act, 1973 inserted
Articles 371D and 371E
to provide constitutional backing for the Six-Point Formula.
The Jai Andhra movement, triggered by the Mulki rules, was called off on
1 October 1973
and subsequently ended with the Six-Point Formula.

Zone I consisted of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam; Zone II of East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone III of Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore; and Zone IV of Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.

The Srikrishna Committee report was issued in December 2010, the Million March occurred at Tank Bund in March 2011, Sakala Janula Samme took place during September–October 2011, and the CWC resolution came in July 2013.

secs.t: Committees → chairman and mandate

x: The Committee on Telangana studied the separate-state demand; the Expert Committee on AP capital was associated with K.C. Sivaramakrishnan and considered capital options; the GN Rao Committee and BCG study formed the basis of the three-capitals plan.
The Thirteenth Schedule included institutions such as IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS, central and tribal universities, and infrastructure proposals including a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.

secs.t: Article 3 - procedure, President's role, current count

x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and to increase or diminish the area, alter the boundaries, or change the name of any State.
A law under Article 3 requires only
a simple majority
in Parliament and is not a constitutional amendment under Article 368 by virtue of Article 4.
The Bill requires the President’s prior recommendation, is referred to the affected State Legislature for its views, and is then dealt with by Parliament.

secs.t: UTs - reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir

x: The 2019 Act reorganised the former State of Jammu and Kashmir into the Union Territories of
Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh
The two Union Territories came into existence on
31 October 2019
The former State Legislature and its Legislative Council were abolished, and Jammu and Kashmir now has a Legislative Assembly as a Union Territory.

secs.t: CM during the agitation and outcome - CM change, fate of the TPS

x: Exam angle: CM in 1969 = Kasu Brahmananda Reddy; CM in Jai Andhra 1972 = P.V. Narasimha Rao. Examiners pair these two.
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
was the Chief Minister during the 1969 Telangana agitation.
Those who opposed the merger of the Telangana Praja Samiti with the Congress formed the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.

secs.t: Causes - safeguard violations alleged (services, revenue, employment)

x: Non-locals were alleged to have been recruited, Telangana’s revenue surplus was allegedly diverted, and the political safeguards were considered unenforceable in court.
The
Gentlemen’s Agreement
of 20 February 1956 included the safeguard that Telangana’s revenue surplus should be spent only in Telangana.
In 1968, the Telangana regional sub-committee was extended for five years and the State requested the Centre to extend the Mulki rules.

secs.t: Start - place, first hunger strike, student bodies

x: The first hunger strike was undertaken by the student
Ravindranath
at Khammam in January 1969.
The regional sub-committee was extended in 1968; the first hunger strike occurred in January 1969; the TPS was formed in February 1969; and the agitation intensified by March 1969.

secs.t: Telangana Praja Samiti - founder, year, 1971 election result

x: Marri Channa Reddy was the president of the Telangana Praja Samiti.
The Telangana Praja Samiti won 10 of the 14 Lok Sabha seats it contested in Telangana in the 1971 election.
Parliament was dissolved on 27 December 1970, Indira Gandhi won a two-thirds majority, and Congress nevertheless lost ground in the Telangana seats.

secs.t: Government responses - Eight-Point Plan, Five-Point Plan, Bhargava, Lalit and Wanchoo committees

x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi at a special meeting in Delhi on
11 April 1969

All eight statements correctly describe the clauses of the Eight-Point Formula, including the six-monthly review by the Prime Minister with Central Ministers and the Planning Commission Vice-Chairman.

The Bhargava Committee assessed Telangana's revenue surpluses, the Lalit Committee undertook official accounting of surplus funds, and the Wanchoo Committee examined the constitutional validity of job safeguards.

secs.t: Supreme Court and High Court on Mulki rules → judgment

x: The October 1972 ruling concerned the older Mulki Rules; the residence clause of the 1957 Act had been struck down in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao in 1969.
In Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy, the Mulki Rules were held valid and still in force, allowing non-locals to be legally barred from public posts in Hyderabad and Telangana.
The correct sequence is 1957 Act, 1969 A.V.S. Narasimha Rao judgment, October 1972 judgment upholding the Mulki Rules, and 1973 repeal under the Six-Point Formula.
The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and replaced by the
zonal system

secs.t: Police firings and casualties - Telangana martyrs

x: Severe police firings during the 1969 movement resulted in the death of
over 360
students and agitators, remembered as the Telangana martyrs.

secs.t: President's rule in AP during the movement → year + duration

x: President's Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh from
18 January 1973 to 10 December 1973
, for approximately eleven months.

secs.t: End of the movement - how and when it ended

x: The Six-Point Formula was proposed on 21 September 1973, the Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973, the agitation was called off on 1 October 1973, and the Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on 1 January 1974.

secs.t: Article 371D and 32nd Amendment → year + provisions

x: Article 371D provided for an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.
Article 371E empowers Parliament to establish
a Central University
in the State, represented by the University at Hyderabad.
The Presidential Order of 1975 created
six zones
to make civil-service recruitment more decentralised and equitable.
Local cadres could be organised district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise, and direct recruitment was reserved for locals of the relevant area.
The Thirty-second Amendment of 1973 gave effect to the Six-Point Formula and inserted Articles 371D and 371E.

secs.t: Leaders of Jai Andhra → role

x: Kakani Venkataratnam
was the prominent Congress leader who spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation.
M. Venkaiah Naidu took part in the Jai Andhra Movement as a
student leader
Student groups
formed the core of the Jai Andhra Movement.

secs.t: Movements for and against Mulki rules → year + region, chronology with GO 610 and Girglani Commission

x: The correct sequence is Jai Telangana agitation (1969), Jai Andhra agitation (1972), 32nd Amendment (1973), GO 610 (1985), and Girglani Report (2004).
The Six-Point Formula of 1973 and the 32nd Amendment represented a compromise after the regional agitations concerning Mulki safeguards.
GO 610 sought to repatriate non-local employees appointed contrary to the 1975 Presidential Order and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.

secs.t: Girglani Commission - year, findings on GO 610 violations

x: The one-man Girglani Commission was constituted in 2001 by the
Chandrababu Naidu
government and submitted its report in 2004.
The commission headed by J.M. Girglani examined violations and highlighted large-scale non-local appointments in Telangana zones, particularly Zone VI.
GO 610
was weakly implemented, leading to the constitution of the Girglani Commission to examine continuing violations of the Presidential Order and GO 610.

secs.t: Mulki rules - origin in Hyderabad State, definition of mulki, residence requirement

x: The Mulki rules originated in
Hyderabad State in 1888
, during the rivalry between Mulki and non-Mulki groups in the Nizam's bureaucracy.
The 1919 Farman required outsiders to obtain the Nizam's personal permission, strengthening the protection of local employment.
The Nizam's rules used a 15-year continuous residence requirement, while the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested domicile rules such as 12 years' residence.

secs.t: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained
Zones I to IV
for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.
Six zones and two multi-zones were approved in April 2026, and final mapping was completed in May 2026.
The district list of Andhra Pradesh's six new zones and two multi-zones for its 26 districts is not provided in the stated material.

secs.t: Polavaram national project, transfer of mandals, SCS, Ramapada Sagaram

x: Special Category Status was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha, not a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act.
The 2014 Amendment Ordinance amended
Section 3
and transferred seven Khammam mandals in the Polavaram submergence area to Andhra Pradesh.
The Ordinance transferred seven specified mandals and retained the Bhurgumpadu villages in Andhra Pradesh; it did not transfer the entire Khammam district.

secs.t: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001, the Centre's announcement followed in December 2009, the Srikrishna Committee report came in December 2010, and the Million March occurred in March 2011.
The Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana was adopted in July 2013, later than the TRS formation in 2001, the Srikrishna Committee report in 2010 and Sakala Janula Samme in 2011.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The movement was significant for making separate statehood a major political issue, and its student-party-central formula sequence was repeated in 2001–2014.
K. Jayashankar was a former Vice-Chancellor of
Kakatiya University
and was widely regarded as the ideologue of the Telangana movement.
The two regional agitations were followed by the Six-Point Formula in 1973 and Article 371D, which provided the constitutional basis for local cadres and related arrangements.
Although the system replaced political assurances with constitutional zoning, disputes over non-local appointments continued, including issues associated with GO 610 and the Girglani Commission.
The Mulki question is traced from
and is linked with the 1969 and 1972 agitations, Article 371D, GO 610 and bifurcation.
Bhatti Vikramarka sought time-bound closure of pending Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act disputes and protection of Telangana's rights relating to Krishna waters.

All four statements are correct according to the stated profile: the 2011 population is 4.96 crore, the Governor is S. Abdul Nazeer, the Chief Minister is N. Chandrababu Naidu and the coastline is described as the second longest.

rows.title: Naxalite movement in Andhra Pradesh - Srikakulam origins, course and impact
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Government responses - Greyhounds, ban, surrender policy, peace talks → year

x: H.J. Dora was DGP from 1996 to 2002, Greyhounds neutralised several top leaders, and over 1,200 cadres surrendered during 1998–2001.
The Anandapuram Greyhounds base is credited with securing the LWE corridor in the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts along the Odisha–Chhattisgarh borders.
The national toolkit includes intelligence-led operations, stronger state police, rehabilitation, dialogue, and development of roads and mobile towers.

secs.t: Srikakulam Girijan struggle - period, tribes, leaders, party that led it

x: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally dated to
, although 1968–69 is also used in some references.
The uprising in the Srikakulam Agency was directed against
landlords, moneylenders and forest officials
Vempatapu Satyam, Adibhatla Kailasam and Subbarao Panigrahi were associated with the Srikakulam struggle.
The struggle was suppressed by the State, but it helped seed the Naxalite movement and revolutionary literature in Andhra.

secs.t: Naxalite groups → founder + year + base state

x: CPI(ML) is associated with Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal; the AP extremist wing with the four Andhra leaders; PWG with Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; and CPI (Maoist) with the PWG–MCC merger.
The CPI (Maoist) emerged in 2004 through the merger of the People’s War Group and the Maoist Communist Centre.
The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing dates to 1967, CPI(ML) to 1969, PWG to 1980, and CPI (Maoist) to 2004.

secs.t: Naxalbari link and CPI(ML) formation → year

x: The Naxalbari uprising of March–May 1967 was led by
Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal
The “Ballot to Bullet” line rejected
the CPI(M)’s parliamentary path
and favoured armed revolutionary struggle.
The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, described India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model strategy of protracted guerrilla war.
Land concentration, failed reforms such as zamindari abolition, ceilings and tenancy reforms, and tribal exploitation were identified as causes.

secs.t: Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam) - founding year, founders

x: Virasam was founded on
4 July 1970
in Hyderabad.
Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam.
The pamphlet was distributed by Andhra University students at
Sri Sri’s 60th-birthday celebrations in Vizag on 1–2 February 1970
Jhamjha, published in 1970, is identified as the first revolutionary poetry collection.

secs.t: Impact on land reforms and tribal areas - ITDAs, Girijan Cooperative Corporation

x: ITDAs were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan, beginning in 1974–75.
The Girijan Cooperative Corporation procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, helping free tribals from moneylenders.
The movement placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics, and Dalits within it later concentrated on land struggles.

secs.t: Emergency period encounters and Bhargava Commission

x: Many Naxalite cadres were killed in alleged encounters in Andhra Pradesh during the Emergency,
The Bhargava Commission, headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava, was set up in 1977 to inquire into alleged encounter killings during the Emergency.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Srikakulam helped make Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.

secs.t: Anti-arrack movement - origin, year, women leaders, prohibition law; 1930s precursor (Kallur Subbarao)

x: Women discussed the effects of men's arrack drinking during Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes, which helped initiate the agitation.
Women used
broomsticks and chilli powder
to close arrack shops, after which the protest spread across Andhra Pradesh.
The literacy lessons enabled women to discuss arrack, debt, domestic violence and the problem of men missing work.

secs.t: Left parties' joint land-occupation campaigns - name, year, parties (Bhu Poratam)

x: Bhu Poratam was jointly launched by the
CPI and CPI(M)
in Andhra Pradesh.
The CPI and CPI(M) launched Bhu Poratam in Andhra Pradesh in 2007.
Bhu Poratam sought the occupation and distribution of
government and surplus land
to landless people.
Bhu Poratam continued the Communist tradition of tenancy and land campaigns carried out during 1956–69.

secs.t: Dalit movement events - Karamchedu, Chunduru → year + district

x: The Karamchedu massacre occurred in
Prakasam
district on 17 July 1985.
The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in
Guntur
district.
After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties and formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.
Katti Padmarao, Manda Krishna Madiga and Endluri Sudhakar are associated with that assertion.

secs.t: Dalit Mahasabha - founder, year

x: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in 1985 after Karamchedu, with Katti Padmarao identified as its founder and Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.
The Adi-Andhra movement was associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, whose Machilipatnam conference took place in 1919.
Kusuma Dharmanna was associated with the 1936 Adi-Andhra Mahasabha held at
Vizianagaram

secs.t: Backward class commissions of AP → chairman + year

x: The Anantharaman Commission, functioning during 1968–70,
was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories
The Muralidhar Rao Commission examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
The commission combined the BC, ST and religious-group populations as
29.08 percent
, contributing to a substantial rise in the State reservation quota.

secs.t: Farmers' and Kisan Sabha movements → founder + issue (N.G. Ranga; power tariff agitation, Bashir Bagh firing)

x: N.G. Ranga
founded the Indian Peasants’ Institute at Nidubrolu in 1933.
The All India Kisan Sabha was one of the mass organisations through which the
CPI
worked.
Left parties and farmers protested electricity tariff hikes introduced under power-sector reforms during the 2000 agitation.
Police opened fire at Bashir Bagh in Hyderabad on 28 August 2000 during the power tariff agitation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: These movements broadened the political arena from the national-movement elite towards caste, gender and class assertion through organisations such as Mahasabhas, MRPS and women’s anti-arrack groups.
Phule’s Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873, and Periyar’s Self-Respect Movement influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders.
Although total prohibition was imposed in 1995, it was later largely abandoned; prohibition was lifted in 1997.

rows.title: Women's movement in Andhra Pradesh, 1956-2014
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Women's organisations → founder + year

x: Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded in 1937, POW in 1974, Stree Shakti Sanghatana in 1978 and Mahila Dakshata Samiti in 1990.
The Andhra Mahila Samakhya and AP Mahila Sangham were two Communist bodies formed after the CPI split in 1964.
The first State women’s Mahasabha was organised by Communist women in 1947.

secs.t: Legislation - Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act → year; women's reservation in local bodies

x: The 1986 Andhra Pradesh amendment gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property, well before the Central amendment of 2005.
Articles 243D(3) and 243T
provide for at least one-third reservation of seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively.
The 73rd and 74th Amendments were enacted in 1992 and provided at least one-third reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities.

secs.t: Feminist journals → editor + year (Bhumika)

x: Bhumika was founded in 1993 and its editor was
Kondaveeti Satyavathi
Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s Janana and Satihita Bodhini promoted women’s education and widow remarriage.

secs.t: Women leaders in AP politics → first posts held

x: Sharda Mukherjee became the first woman Governor of Andhra Pradesh in 1977.
Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1999.
The relevant years are 1953 for D, 1977 for C, 1986 for A and 1999 for B. Therefore, the sequence is D, C, A, B—not option a.

secs.t: Campaigns - dowry deaths, Joginis, Devadasi abolition → law + year

x: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in 1988.
The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference, associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, demanded abolition of the
Jogini and Devadasi systems
Muthulakshmi Reddy’s campaign was followed by Ammannaraja’s 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly.
NCRB recorded
about 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The movement moved from reform bodies such as Andhra Mahila Sabha to Left and autonomous groups, then to mass action such as Anti-arrack and SHG-based economic activity.
One Stop Centres cover all 26 districts, the 181 helpline has run since 2016, there are 28 Shakti Sadans, and BBBP covers all 26 districts.

rows.title: Important cultural events between 1956 and 2014 - literature, journalism, theatre and cinema
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Cultural institutions established - year and inaugurated by

x: Nataka Vidyalayam of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad
was established at Vijayawada on 1 August 1964 for training in drama.
Sangeet Natak Akademi was the first national arts academy and was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad.
The Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1952, Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1953, Lalit Kala Akademi in 1954, and Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1985.

secs.t: World Telugu Conferences - venue and year

x: Exam angle: the first conference year (1975) is asked repeatedly; it is also the year of the International Telugu Institute.
The First Conference was held at Hyderabad, the Second at Kuala Lumpur, the Third in Mauritius and the Fourth at Tirupati.
The Fourth World Telugu Conference was held at Tirupati in 2012, not at Vijayawada.

secs.t: Newspapers launched - founder and year

x: Andhra Jyothi was founded by K.L.N. Prasad, Eenadu by Ramoji Rao, Udayam by Dasari Narayana Rao and Sakshi by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
Andhra Jyothi was launched in 1960, Eenadu in Visakhapatnam in 1974, and Sakshi in 2008.
Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal, while Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence.

secs.t: Kendra Sahitya Akademi and Padma awards to Telugu figures

x: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1965 for
Misra Manjari
C. Narayana Reddy received the Telugu Velugu award for literature, while Bapu received it for painting.
The Sahitya Akademi Award covers 24 languages—22 Eighth Schedule languages along with English and Rajasthani—and carries Rs 1 lakh.
Jashuva received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964 and the Padma Bhushan in 1970.

secs.t: Cinema milestones - Nandi Awards, Dadasaheb Phalke awardees

x: Nandi Awards are Andhra Pradesh Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.
B.N. Reddy, Akkineni Nageswara Rao and K. Viswanath are among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award.
All three statements are correct for the 71st National Film Awards relating to films of 2023.
The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969, and Devika Rani was its first recipient.

secs.t: Cultural bodies abolished or restructured

x: In 1985, the NTR Government merged the State akademis into the newly established
Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University
The coalition government revived the Kandukuri Awards and announced the revival of the Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The annual Telugu Mahotsavam was announced at the
Undavalli Caves
in July 2026 by Minister Kandula Durgesh.
The festival was scheduled for 15 July 2026 at 150 locations in connection with 150 years of Vande Mataram, with two Andhra Pradesh plays selected.

rows.title: Development of Telugu literature after 1956 - Digambara, Viplava, Dalit, feminist and Muslim minority streams
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Dalit literature anthologies and poets - editor/author (Mallepoddu, Chikkanavutunna Pata, Padunekkina Pata, Nallapoddu)

x: Chikkanavutunna Pata was edited by G. Lakshmi Narasaiah and Tripuraneni Srinivas.
Chikkanavutunna Pata is a 1995 Dalit poetry anthology, while Padunekkina Pata is a 1996 Dalit poetry anthology.
Gurram Jashuva is regarded as the first modern Telugu Dalit poet.
The Karamchedu incident took place in 1985.
Ditta Pullayya is associated with Adi Andhra Patrika.

secs.t: Novels and story collections - author and stream

x: Exam angle: author-work matching; distractors Tulasidalam, Mahaprasthanam, Vennello Aadapilla sit beside Veyi Padagalu.
Veyi Padagalu, Athadu Adavini Jayinchadu, Ramayana Vishavruksham and Tulasidalam are associated respectively with Viswanatha Satyanarayana, Kesava Reddy, Ranganayakamma and Yandamuri Veerendranath.
Ramayana Vishavruksham by Ranganayakamma is described as a
Marxist-feminist critique of the Ramayana
P.V. Narasimha Rao
translated Veyi Padagalu into Hindi as Sahasraphan.

secs.t: Jnanpith awardees in Telugu and translations

x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja received the Jnanpith Award in 1970, 1988 and 2012 respectively.
Viswambhara is associated with C. Narayana Reddy.
Viswanatha Satyanarayana was known as ‘Abhinava Nannaya’ and wrote over 100 works.
N. Chandrababu Naidu recalled all three Telugu Jnanpith awardees at the
World Telugu Mahasabhalu
on 6 January 2026.

secs.t: Protest poems - central image or messenger (Gabbilam, Firdausi)

x: In Gabbilam, a bat carries the message of a hungry Dalit to Lord Shiva.
Gabbilam was modelled on
Kalidasa’s Meghaduta
, in which a messenger carries a message.
Firdausi is Jashuva’s poem about the Persian poet who was cheated of his promised reward by Sultan Mahmud.

secs.t: Digambara kavulu - members, pen names, collections, year

x: The Digambara kavulu were associated with an anti-establishment movement of ‘naked poets’.
The Digambara movement began in 1965, and its three volumes of Digambara Kavitvam appeared during

All four pen names are correctly matched with their real names: Nagnamuni–Manikonda Hanumantha Rao, Nikhileswar–Kumbham Yadava Reddy, Cherabandaraju–Baddam Bhaskara Reddy and Jwalamukhi–Veeravalli Raghavacharyulu.
Cherabandaraju, Jwalamukhi and Nikhileswar
moved on to Virasam in 1970.

secs.t: Viplava sahityam - Virasam founding, key poets and works

x: Viplava Rachayitala Sangham, or Virasam, was founded on
4 July 1970
The formation of Virasam was triggered by a pamphlet issued by Visakhapatnam students titled
‘Writers, where do you stand?’
Maha Prasthanam
broke conventional Telugu prosody and presented a call to the oppressed.
The Srikakulam peasant struggle of 1969 under Vempatapu Satyam helped spread
Naxalism
in Andhra.

secs.t: Feminist poetry - anthologies (Neelimeghalu), editor, key poets

x: Neeli Meghalu, published in 1993, is
an anthology of Telugu feminist poetry
Neeli Meghalu was edited by
Volga and others
Jayaprabha, Vimala and Kondepudi Nirmala
are among the poets associated with Neeli Meghalu.
The spoken-Telugu revolution associated with Gidugu and Gurajada laid the linguistic foundation on which feminist and Dalit fiction developed.

secs.t: Muslim minority literature - anthologies (Jaljala, Puttumacha), editor, poets

x: Puttumacha, meaning ‘Birthmark’, is a long poem by
Khadar Mohiuddin
on Muslim identity.
Jaljala is
an anthology of Telugu Muslim minority poetry of the 1990s

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Post-1956 Telugu literary streams broadened the subject matter of literature to include
caste, class, gender and minority identity
, moving beyond classical and romantic themes.
Digambara, Viplava, Dalit, feminist and Muslim minority streams are all identified as important post-1956 developments in Telugu literature.
Kalyani Thakur Charal is a Bengali Dalit poet, and her translated anthology won the A.K. Ramanujan Prize.

secs.t: Film studios and studio cities - founder, place, year

x: Vijaya Vauhini Studios was founded by B.
Nagi Reddy and Aluri Chakrapani
Annapurna Studios is located in
Hyderabad
Ramanaidu
Studios was founded by D. Ramanaidu.
Guinness lists Ramoji Film City as the world’s largest
film studio complex
The industry’s post-1956 movement from Madras to Hyderabad helped build the
Hyderabad studio belt

secs.t: First Telugu films - year and director

x: Bhishma Pratigna was released in 1921, Bhakta Prahlada in 1931 and Lava Kusa in 1963.
Bhishma Pratigna, the first Telugu silent film, was directed by
Raghupathi Venkaiah Naidu and R.S. Prakash
H.M. Reddy assisted Ardeshir Irani on Alam Ara.
Bhakta Prahlada was the first Telugu talkie, and Ramoji Film City dates from 1996.

secs.t: Film personalities - awards and political careers

x: The correct order is B.N. Reddy (1974), Akkineni Nageswara Rao (1990), D. Ramanaidu (2009), and K. Viswanath (2016).
Mohanlal
received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023 at the 71st National Film Awards in September 2025.
The award was instituted in 1969, first given to Devika Rani, and carries a Swarna Kamal, shawl and cash prize, which was raised to Rs 15 lakh in 2024.

secs.t: Mythological and social film trends - directors

x: K.V. Reddy
directed the mythological and folklore classics Pathala Bhairavi and Mayabazar.
B.N. Reddy
was known for social and lyrical films, including Malliswari.
N.T. Rama Rao’s portrayals of Rama and Krishna in mythological films built his
mass image

secs.t: Actors turned politicians - party and post

x: K. Pawan Kalyan is associated with the Jana Sena Party and became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
The Telugu Desam Party was founded when
Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy
was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
The Telugu Desam Party’s slogan was
Telugu Vari Atma Gauravam
Praja Rajyam was founded by Chiranjeevi, merged with Congress in 2011, and TRS was founded in 2001.

secs.t: Nandi Awards - instituted by, year, categories

x: The Nandi Awards cover
films, television and drama
, including Nandi Natakotsavam for drama.
Nandi Natakotsavam is the
drama
-related component of the Nandi Awards framework.
The Nandi Awards lapsed under the previous government, and their revival was announced in 2026.

secs.t: Television and mass media - Doordarshan Hyderabad, private Telugu channels

x: Gemini TV and ETV
were private Telugu satellite television channels launched in 1995.
ETV is associated with
Ramoji Rao
; Gemini TV and ETV both date from 1995 in the given context.
Prasar Bharati comprises
Akashvani
and Doordarshan.
The National Film Awards are administered by the
National Film Development Corporation
, or NFDC.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Telugu cinema also influenced mass politics, especially through N.T. Rama Rao and the TDP.
Article 370
was selected as the Best Feature Film at the 72nd National Film Awards.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Modern painters of AP - style and titles

x: Exam angle: the "Father of Modern Contemporary Art" PYQ lists Bapiraju, Papaiah and Bapu as distractors.
Damerla Rama Rao was a pioneer of modern Andhra painting associated with
Rajahmundry
, where an art gallery named after him is located.
Bapu was known for his line drawings of epic characters, worked as an illustrator and film director, and received the Telugu Velugu award for painting in Ugadi 2012.

secs.t: Artists' birth names and pen names

x: Bapu’s birth name is Sattiraju Lakshminarayana, whereas Paidi Raju is not his birth name.
Mullapudi Venkata
Ramana
used the name Ramana and was Bapu’s film partner.
Vaddadi Papaiah
was known by the pen name Vapa.

secs.t: Museums of AP - location and collections

x: The Salar Jung Museum at Hyderabad contains the collection of Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, also known as Salar Jung III, gathered over more than 40 years.
The ‘Veiled Rebecca’ marble statue was bought in Rome in 1876 and is part of the Salar Jung Museum collection.
The
Nagarjunakonda island museum
, located in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir, houses archaeological material rescued from the submerged area, including Ikshvaku-Buddhist finds.

secs.t: Archaeological excavations after 1956 - site and excavator

x: The excavation of
Nagarjunakonda
involved Longhurst, Ramachandran and R. Subrahmanyam after its discovery by A. Ranganatha Saraswati.
Thotlakonda
was spotted by the Indian Navy and excavated by the Andhra Pradesh State Archaeology Department.
Nagarjunakonda is associated with Palnadu, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda with Visakhapatnam, and Salihundam with Srikakulam.
Salihundam
in Srikakulam was a Mahayana–Vajrayana port known for Tara bronzes and a Buddha footprint.

secs.t: Heritage sites in AP - UNESCO tentative list, ASI protection

x: Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed World Heritage Site.
The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act is from 1958.

secs.t: Architecture - public buildings and dam-submergence relocation

x: The area was submerged after 1960 because of the Nagarjunasagar Dam project.
The monuments dismantled and rebuilt on higher ground because of Nagarjunasagar Dam submergence are called
Transplanted Monuments
Ravindra Bharathi auditorium in Hyderabad was constructed in 1961 as part of the observance of the Tagore centenary.

secs.t: Department of Archaeology and Museums AP - year founded

x: The department traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department established in 1914.
The Commissioner’s office of the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums is located at
Vijayawada
The Divi Pump Scheme at Puligadda was restored as an irrigation museum in 2014, with about Rs 27 lakh spent of Rs 30 lakh, but was later neglected for lack of funds.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Archaeological Survey of India began scientific conservation of the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple at Mangalagiri.
The “Discover Andhra” campaign promotes a Buddhist heritage circuit comprising
Amaravati, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda
The
division of museum antiques
remained one of the unfinished items arising from the 2014 bifurcation.
Cosmetic restoration is criticised for failing to protect the authentic historical character of heritage sites.

rows.title: Post-independence consolidation - land reforms, tribal and border policy, national integration
sub: Group-II M1-A-115: Important social events between 1956 and 2014 - reform, welfare and legislation

secs.t: Bhoodan and Gramdan - founder, village and state of origin

x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave began the Bhoodan Movement at
Pochampalli
on 18 April 1951.
Vedire Ramachandra Reddy was the first donor and donated 100 acres of land.
Gramdan was the next stage of Bhoodan in which an entire village was gifted to the community.
Mangroth in Hamirpur district of Uttar Pradesh was the first Gramdan village in 1952.

secs.t: Integration of Portuguese and French enclaves

x: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated through Operation Vijay, while Pondicherry was a French enclave.
Goa, Daman and Diu
remained under Portuguese control until 19 December 1961, when Operation Vijay ended Portuguese rule there.
Dadra and Nagar Haveli became a Union Territory under the Tenth Amendment, Goa, Daman and Diu under the Twelfth Amendment, and Goa attained statehood in 1987.

secs.t: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry

x: The Act required written lease deeds, prescribed leases of at least six years and came into force in 1961.
The Telangana tenancy law was passed in the context of
the Telangana armed struggle
The tenant could purchase ownership at 60 per cent of the market price in
20 instalments
The Samatha judgment of 1997 barred leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals and private mining firms.

secs.t: National integration - NIC, origin, official language debate

x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the
National Integration Conference
The conference considered
communalism, casteism, regionalism and linguism
as threats to national integration.
The Official Languages Act of 1963 continued the use of English for official purposes along with Hindi.
Tamil Nadu retained the two-language formula after anti-Hindi agitations associated with 1937, 1965 and 1986.

secs.t: Land reform phases

x: The practice of ‘
voluntary surrenders
’ enabled landlords to evade the protection intended by tenancy reforms.
Operation Barga, introduced in West Bengal in 1977, was an important exception to the general failure of tenancy reform.
Abolition of intermediaries
is a recognised component of land reforms, along with tenancy reform, ceiling, consolidation, cooperative farming and computerisation of land records.
Raj Krishna grouped land reforms as
liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental

secs.t: Tribal policy - Tribal Panchsheel, Fifth and Sixth Schedules, Verrier Elwin

x: Nehru rejected both the museum approach of isolation and forced assimilation, favouring integration while respecting tribal identity and institutions.
The formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin under the influence of Jawaharlal Nehru.
PESA 1996 applies to Scheduled Areas in states covered by the Fifth Schedule; it does not apply to the Sixth Schedule autonomous district areas.

secs.t: Border and North-East policy - NEFA, Naga question

x: NEFA was run through the
Governor of Assam
and served as a policy laboratory for Elwin's approach.
NEFA was first administered through the Governor of Assam, became a Union Territory in 1972 and became a state in 1987.
The Centre addressed the Naga question in 1963 by creating the state of Nagaland.

secs.t: Abolition of intermediaries - Act and year (Andhra area, Telangana area)

x: The Andhra Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was enacted in 1956.
Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after the abolition measures.
The
Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act
abolished zamindari in the Andhra area.
Implementation of the Abolition of Telangana Inams Act, 1955 was
stalled in the courts

secs.t: Welfare schemes - CM and year

x: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme, along with subsidised housing and Janata cloth, was associated with N.T. Rama Rao and introduced in 1983.
Janmabhoomi was introduced in 1997 under
N. Chandrababu Naidu
and emphasised people's participation in development.
The
Fee Reimbursement
scheme, introduced in 2008, supported higher education for poor students and was associated with Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

secs.t: Education landmarks - residential schools, universities

x: The first residential school was established at Sarvail in
Nalgonda
The Andhra Pradesh Open University, now named Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University, was the first open university in India and was established in 1982.
NTR University of Health Sciences
, established in 1986, was the first health university in India.

secs.t: Social legislation - Devadasi, Jogini, prohibition

x: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in 1988 and also covered Jogini, Basivi and Matangi dedication.
The Dubagunta movement occurred in 1992, the arrack ban in 1993, total prohibition under N.T. Rama Rao in 1995 and lifting of prohibition in 1997.
N.T. Rama Rao
imposed total prohibition in 1995, after the 1993 arrack ban under Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy.

secs.t: Reservation and BC policy milestones

x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission was associated with 1982; NTR raised the BC quota to 44 percent in 1986, and the High Court struck down the enhanced quota.
The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was implemented through Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.
The 2007 reservation for backward Muslims was associated with the
BC-E
category and amounted to 4 percent.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Vibrant Villages Programme-II covers 1,954 villages in 15 States and 2 Union Territories along the borders with Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Myanmar.
The Bhoodan Movement began at Pochampalli in the
Telugu country
, making it an important Andhra-related land reform milestone.
The Eluru agency land dispute involves
APSALT Regulation 1/59 and Regulation 1/70
, showing that tribal land law remains subject to litigation.

rows.title: Tribal culture of Andhra - major tribes, social organisation, festivals, dances and art forms
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-216

secs.t: Tribal festivals → tribe

x: Eetela Panduga or Chaitrapurab is
the spring festival of the Araku tribes
, during which Dhimsa is danced.
Seethala Panduga
is a Lambadi festival observed in Ashada.
